correctness.rationale: The unweighted Bergman kernel and mixed derivative formula are checked directly. Applying (1+a∂z+b∂z²/2) and its conjugate gives exactly K(z,w)[1+6(b-a²)t²+30b²t⁴], t=(z-w̄)^(-1). The latter map surjects onto the open lower half-plane by an explicit construction. The quadratic in x=t² has discriminant 36[(a²-b)²-(10/3)b²]. For all real a,b its nonnegative-discriminant branch is equivalent to a²≥b+√(10/3)|b| and yields only positive x roots; the negative branch yields two simple lower roots. The b=0 and equality cases are handled separately, so the exact universal theorem is proved. Independent symbolic differentiation of the operator matches the factorial expansion and CHECK.py completes 4313 supplementary assertions, not relied on as proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Our theorem adds an if-and-only-if zero-free inequality, exact two-scalar-zero count below it, and double boundary roots, for every real pair (a,b). Gehlawat--Jain--Sarkar yield the polynomial from which it can be calculated, but do not establish these implications. The published two-jet result gives b=0 zero-freeness and the separated-jet result gives a=0 nonzero zeros; they do not settle whether and exactly when the middle jet repairs the separated two-jet zeros. The conditional negative and positive examples show that such an implication would need a new three-term comparison.

value.rationale: For the first natural complete real three-jet family beyond existing two-term classifications, the theorem determines the entire sharp zero-free parameter region and a boundary-root collision. A separated value-plus-second-derivative jet has zeros for every nonzero second coefficient, yet adding the first derivative can remove all of them above a sign-sensitive exact threshold. This is a motivated structural restoration phenomenon for the newly introduced canonical kernel, not an arbitrary isolated parameter or routine recomputation of a known table. Its scope and elementary proof are explicitly acknowledged.
